# CodeTour generation

This skill creates a real Tour file in the workspace with the `codetour` CLI.
The proposal travels on standard input, the CLI validates it against the
workspace, writes the Tour atomically, and answers with one JSON document. A
Tour is never written by hand and never replaced by prose.

`codetour` on `PATH` is the documented default, and no Copilot surface supplies
a launcher argument. The reference modules beside this file spell the CLI
`<cli>`; in this skill `<cli>` is `codetour`.

## 1. Resolve the choices

Honor what the user already said: "review my branch critically" means a Changes
Tour with `reviewMode: "critical"`, and nothing is asked twice. Ask only for
what is missing, once per question, and stop without generating if the user
cancels or declines; never silently default.

- **Type** — a **Project Tour** (architecture, structure and execution paths)
  or a **Changes Tour** (explain and review the branch's changes).
- **Review mode** — Changes Tours only: `neutral` (factual explanation) or
  `critical` (explanation plus review findings). Project Tours have none.
- **Orientation and language** — a phrase that orients the Tour ("focus on the
  rendering pipeline") is optional; it also sets the language the Tour is
  written in. Without one, write the Tour in the language of the user's request.

A Tour takes exactly one of three paths, and each has its own reference module
beside this file. Once the type and the review mode are known, state the module
path you selected, then read that module **before exploring** and keep it read
while you write: it carries that path's route, its proposal fields and its
creation command, and it completes the shared rules below without repeating
them.

| Path | Module |
| --- | --- |
| **Project Tour** | [references/project-tour.md](references/project-tour.md) |
| **Changes Tour**, `neutral` | [references/changes-tour-neutral.md](references/changes-tour-neutral.md) |
| **Changes Tour**, `critical` | [references/changes-tour-critical.md](references/changes-tour-critical.md) |

Only the critical module carries the review pack of a critical Changes Tour. On
a Project Tour or a neutral Changes Tour, do not open that pack: nothing it says
applies to them.

Whatever the path, read the entry points and the main modules, not just the file
names, and base every statement on the code you read.

## 2. Work in the workspace root

Every command runs at the workspace root, and `--workspace` receives that root
as an absolute path (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, or the directory the user
named). One creation addresses one workspace: every anchor and the Tour file
itself stay inside it.

## 3. Build the proposal

### Mermaid diagrams

When adding a Mermaid diagram, read and follow [the Mermaid reference](references/mermaid.md) before building the proposal.

### Anchors

When adding anchors, read and follow [the anchor reference](references/anchors.md) before submitting the proposal.

One JSON object, with the fields the CLI validates:

- `title` (optional: the CLI defaults a Project Tour to `Project Overview` and
  a Changes Tour to `Changes on <branch>`), `description`, `fileName` (a bare
  name, written under `.tours/`), `steps` (at least one).
- A step carries a `title`, a Markdown `description`, and optionally one anchor:
  `file` with either `line` or `pattern`, `directory`, `selection`
  (`{start: {line, character}, end: {...}}`), `display: "diff"` with
  `baseFile`. A step without an anchor is explanatory, which is what the
  orientation step should be.
- `questions` (at most four short strings) attach the questions the reader
  should answer at that step.

Explore the workspace before proposing anything and verify each anchor against
the applicable file version as described in the anchor reference.

With `includeUncommittedChanges` left at `false`, the Tour compares committed
state only: ground every claim in the committed diff and the files at `headRef`,
not the current working tree — dirty or untracked files can contain newer
behavior. From the workspace, read committed files with
`git show <headRef>:./<workspace-relative-path>` and compare with the merge-base
where needed. Never describe an excluded local change as committed, even if it
appears in the current skill or project files.

### The comparison and the refs

A Changes Tour describes exactly one range, and it is fixed before exploring.
`baseRef` and `headRef` are mandatory for every Changes Tour, and `headRef` is
the full 40-character SHA of the analysed HEAD commit, never an abbreviation.
Resolve them before writing the document: `git rev-parse HEAD` for `headRef`,
`git merge-base <base> HEAD` for a `baseRef` the user gave as a branch.
`includeUncommittedChanges` is `false` unless the local changes belong to the
comparison, and `reviewMode` is `neutral` or `critical`; the module of the path
shows the complete document of that path.

When the user gave no context, `gh pr view --json title,body,baseRefName,url` or
the `glab` equivalent describes the pull request; say what you used, and never
invent a title, a goal or a finding.

## 4. Hand the proposal over

````sh
codetour create-project-tour --workspace "<absolute workspace root>" <<'JSON'
{"title": "…", "steps": [{"title": "…", "description": "…"}]}
JSON

codetour create-changes-tour --workspace "<absolute workspace root>" <<'JSON'
{
  "title": "Changes on feature/payments",
  "description": "What the branch changes, and what the review establishes.",
  "baseRef": "9f1c2d3e4b5a60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9012345ab",
  "headRef": "4a7d6f2c1b0e9d8c7b6a5f4e3d2c1b0a99887766",
  "includeUncommittedChanges": false,
  "reviewMode": "critical",
  "steps": [{ "title": "…", "description": "…" }]
}
JSON
````

`--proposal <file>` reads the proposal from a file instead of standard input;
both carry the same document.

Exit codes say what happened:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | the Tour was created; standard output holds the result document |
| `1` | the proposal, its validation or the creation was refused |
| `2` | usage or IO failure: missing or unknown argument, unusable workspace, unreadable proposal, explicit `--help` |

Standard output carries exactly one JSON document whenever a creation is
attempted, and a usage answer (`--help`, exit `2`) leaves it empty. Standard
error carries diagnostics only.

## 5. Handle the result

Success (`{"ok": true, …}`) reports `kind`, `title`, `tourPath` (absolute),
`stepCount` and `warnings`. Report the title and the path to the user, and read
the warnings: they are readability advice, not failures.

Refusal (`{"ok": false, "code": …, "message": …, "issues": [...]}`) wrote
nothing: fix **every** `issues` entry (`path` names the field, `message` says
what is wrong), then resubmit the corrected proposal. Do not retry the same
document and do not lower the Tour's quality to get past a validation.

Exit code `2` means the command line itself was unusable (a missing
`--workspace`, an unknown option, an unreadable proposal file). Report the
diagnostic; do not retry it blindly.

If `codetour` is missing, say so and stop: the generation needs the CLI on
`PATH`, and `codetour --install copilot` reinstalls this plugin when the skill
itself is missing. A text answer is not a Tour.

## 6. Hand the Tour over to a reader

Never replace the created Tour with a step list, an excerpt or a summary. Offer
the real readers, to run at the workspace root:

- Terminal — `codetour "<Tour title>"`, or
  `codetour --internal-tour "<tour path>"` to open the file directly;
- VS Code — `codetour --internal-open-vscode "<tour path>"`, which opens the
  Tour at its first step.

A reading failure is reported with the command to run manually; it never
invalidates the Tour that was created.

src/cli/pi-plugin.generated.ts:10:  "README.md": "# CodeTour Pi plugin

This directory is the versioned **Pi package** source of the CodeTour
integration for the Pi coding agent. It is embedded in the standalone CodeTour
CLI and installed by:

```sh
codetour --install pi
```

A plain `pi install ./packages/pi-plugin` installs the same directory directly;
`pi remove ./packages/pi-plugin` removes it. The managed install writes
`launcher.json` so the session uses the CLI that performed the installation
instead of whatever `codetour` happens to be on `PATH`.

## Contents

| Path | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `package.json` | Pi package manifest (`pi.extensions`, `pi.skills`, peer dependency on the host). |
| `extensions/codetour.ts` | `/codetour` (generate or read a Tour) and the end-of-response report: the Tours the response created, then its token reading. |
| `lib/journal.mjs` | Reads the creation journal and attributes a creation to a response; the token reading and the summary lines. |
| `lib/reader.mjs` | The end-of-generation opening dialogue: the real interactive reader (terminal) or the Tour at its active step (VS Code). |
| `skills/codetour-generate/SKILL.md` | The generation entry point: the agent explores the workspace and creates the Tour with the CLI. |
| `skills/codetour-generate/references/` | The path modules the skill reads before exploring (`project-tour.md`, `changes-tour-neutral.md`, `changes-tour-critical.md`), the Mermaid and anchor guidance, and the critical-review pack only the critical module carries: the CodeTour adaptation, the verbatim upstream skill and its MIT license. |

## No server, no checkout

The package needs neither a server nor a CodeTour repository. The skill explores
the workspace the session is in and calls the installed CodeTour CLI from the
workspace root:

```sh
codetour create-project-tour --workspace . --proposal -
codetour create-changes-tour --workspace . --proposal -
```

The proposal is one JSON document on standard input (or in a file passed to
`--proposal`); the result is one JSON document on standard output, with exit
code `0` for a created Tour, `1` for a rejected proposal and `2` for a usage or
IO failure. A rejected proposal lists the `issues` to correct and writes
nothing.

The extension passes the CLI it knows as the skill argument
`codetour-cli=["<command>","<args>"…]` (the recorded launcher); without that
argument the skill uses `codetour` from `PATH`.

## `/codetour`

`/codetour` opens the native Pi menu **Generate / Read**. **Read** lists the
workspace Tours and plays the selected Tour in Pi's terminal. Press `q` to
return to Pi. Use `/codetour read "Tour title"` to open a Tour directly.

**Generate** collects the choices (Project Tour, or Changes Tour with a neutral
or critical review), then delivers
`/skill:codetour-generate type=… [reviewMode=…] [codetour-cli=…] [request=…]`
to the agent. No run state is written and no server is registered: the agent
creates the Tour itself with the CLI. A cancelled choice starts nothing.

## The end-of-response report

When a response settles (`agent_settled`), the extension reads
`<workspace>/.tours/.log/creations/` — the journal the CLI writes after every
successful creation — and reports, once per response:

- one line per Tour created **by this response**: title and path;
- one token reading for the response: `input`, `output`, `cache`, with
  `(approximate)` when the scope is not exact and `unavailable` when the host
  reports nothing.

The report never blocks, never asks for a continuation, never calls a model and
never changes the exit status. It has nothing to say when no creation is
attributed, and it prints at most one token reading per response.

Attribution requires the same canonical workspace, the same session identity
(the CLI's `PI_SESSION_ID` equals `ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId()`), and a
creation record not older than the response's `agent_start`. A creation without
a session identity is never reported; an unreadable or foreign journal entry is
ignored.

Verified limits of this surface (Pi 1.6.0):

- **The report is visible in the interactive TUI only.** It goes through
  `ctx.ui.notify`; in `-p` and `--mode json` the host gives extensions a no-op
  UI context (`ctx.hasUI === false`), and no extension API writes to stdout. The
  creation itself is unaffected.
- **Pi has no response identity.** There is no `PI_RESPONSE_ID`, and the
  extension context carries no run id, so the response boundary is the
  `agent_start` timestamp compared with each record's `at`. `responseId` stays
  `null` in the journal; the extension never invents one.
- **Only creations made through the agent's shell tool are attributable.**
  `pi.exec()` does not export `PI_SESSION_ID`, so a child spawned by the
  extension has no session identity — the skill must run the creation command
  through its shell tool.
- **Sub-agent sessions are not attributable**: the sub-agent's shell exports the
  sub-agent's `PI_SESSION_ID`, while the parent hook sees the parent session, so
  the report stays silent instead of attributing the creation to the wrong
  session.
- Token figures come from the `Usage` of the assistant messages of the response
  (`agent_end`); some providers report all-zero usage, which is shown as
  unavailable, never as zero. `input` already excludes the cache, so `cache`
  (`cacheRead + cacheWrite`) is never added twice.

## The opening dialogue

When a Tour is attributed to the response, the extension reports it and then
asks the user how to open it — never a step list or a summary in the Tour's
place:

- **Terminal** — the real interactive reader, spawned at once from the managed
  launcher (the `launcher.json` CLI, not whatever `codetour` happens to be on
  `PATH`): `codetour --internal-tour "<tour path>"` (or the default reading path
  on the recorded title). The spawn inherits the session's terminal — never a
  PTY or an independent window — the extension waits for the reading to end,
  then the terminal is back with the session. A non-interactive session or a
  failed spawn degrades to the documented hand-over command, never a crash.
- **VS Code** — the managed launcher executes
  `--internal-open-vscode "<tour path>"` at the workspace root: the
  Open-in-VS Code contract of ticket #244, the Tour at its active step. The
  decision lives once in the CLI's `openInVscode` module; a failure is reported
  with a manual command.

The ask is once per created Tour; a declined ask hands over nothing and leaves
no substitute text.

## Requirements

- A Pi version that supports package manifests with `pi.skills` and
  `pi.extensions`, `registerCommand`, `agent_start` / `agent_end` /
  `agent_settled`, and `ctx.ui.notify`.
- The CodeTour CLI: the managed install records its absolute path in
  `launcher.json` and passes it to the skill; a direct `pi install` of this
  source expects `codetour` on `PATH`.
- No Node subprocess and no extra hook runtime: everything runs inside Pi. The
  CLI is run by the agent's shell tool, as part of the generation it performs.

const root = path.resolve(__dirname, "..");

function walk(directory, prefix = "") {
  const entries = [];
  for (const entry of fs.readdirSync(directory, { withFileTypes: true }).sort((left, right) => left.name.localeCompare(right.name))) {
    const relative = prefix ? `${prefix}/${entry.name}` : entry.name;
    if (entry.isDirectory()) entries.push(...walk(path.join(directory, entry.name), relative));
    else if (entry.isFile()) entries.push(relative);
  }
  return entries;
}

function walk(directory, prefix = "") {
  const entries = [];
  for (const entry of fs.readdirSync(directory, { withFileTypes: true }).sort((left, right) => left.name.localeCompare(right.name))) {
    const relative = prefix ? `${prefix}/${entry.name}` : entry.name;
    if (entry.node_modules || entry.name === "node_modules") continue;
    if (entry.isDirectory()) entries.push(...walk(path.join(directory, entry.name), relative));
    else if (entry.isFile()) entries.push(relative);
  }
  return entries;

export class URIHandler implements vscode.UriHandler {
  private _didStartDefaultTour = false;
  get didStartDefaultTour(): boolean {
    return this._didStartDefaultTour;
  }

  async handleUri(uri: vscode.Uri): Promise<void> {
    const target = new URLSearchParams(uri.query).get("workspace");
    if (uri.path === "/openTour" && target) {
      const expected = canonicalWorkspacePath(target);
      const matches = vscode.workspace.workspaceFolders?.some(folder =>
        folder.uri.scheme === "file" && canonicalWorkspacePath(folder.uri.fsPath) === expected
      );
      if (!matches) {
        void vscode.window.showErrorMessage("This tour link was sent to a different workspace. Open the intended workspace and retry.");
        return;
      }
    }
    this._didStartDefaultTour = true;
    await discoverTours();

    let query = uri.query;
    if (uri.path === "/startDefaultTour") {
      query = vscode.Uri.parse(uri.query).query;
    }

    if (query) {
      const params = new URLSearchParams(query);
      startTour(params);
    } else {
      startDefaultTour();
    }
  }

async function renderCurrentStep(forceCurrentFile = false) {
  const version = ++renderVersion;
  if (store.activeTour!.thread) {
    store.activeTour!.thread.dispose();
    store.activeTour!.thread = null;
  }

  const currentTour = store.activeTour!.tour;
  const currentStep = store.activeTour!.step;

  const step = currentTour!.steps[currentStep];
  if (!step) {
    return;
  }

  const workspaceRoot = store.activeTour?.workspaceRoot;
  let diff = forceCurrentFile ? undefined : await getStepDiff(step, currentTour, workspaceRoot);
  let uri = diff?.modified || await getStepFileUri(
    step, workspaceRoot, step.display === "diff" ? undefined : currentTour.ref
  );
  let unavailableFile = false;
  let document: TextDocument | undefined;
  let line = step.line
    ? step.line - 1
    : step.selection
    ? step.selection.end.line - 1
    : undefined;

  // The existing fallback when a step's target cannot be opened: the reader
  // is warned, the step stays readable and the tour continues.
  const markUnavailableFile = () => {
    unavailableFile = true;
    line = 0;
    uri = CONTENT_URI;
    if (version === renderVersion) {
      window.showWarningMessage(
        `CodeTour: file unavailable: ${step.file || step.uri}. You can continue the tour.`
      );
    }
  };

  if (step.display === "diff" && step.file) {
    try {
      document = await workspace.openTextDocument(uri);
    } catch {
      diff = undefined;
      uri = await getStepFileUri(step, workspaceRoot);
      try {
        document = await workspace.openTextDocument(uri);
      } catch {
        markUnavailableFile();
      }
    }
  }
  if (version !== renderVersion || !store.activeTour || !controller) return;

  if (step.file && !unavailableFile && line === undefined) {
    const stepPattern = step.pattern || getActiveStepMarker();
    if (stepPattern) {
      try {
        document = document || await workspace.openTextDocument(uri);
        const match = document.getText().match(new RegExp(stepPattern, "m"));
        if (match) {
          line = document.positionAt(match.index!).line;
        }
      } catch (error) {
        if (!isWebviewPlayback()) {
          throw error;
        }
        if (version !== renderVersion || !store.activeTour) {
          return;
        }
        // In webview mode a missing pattern host keeps the step readable in
        // the panel instead of breaking the render.
        markUnavailableFile();
      }
    }
  }

  // independent terminal window (ticket #241). Only an explicit
  // --renderer html opens the browser page.
  if (renderer === "vscode") {
    await openTourInVsCode({ tourId: tour.id, workspaceRoot: root, step: 0 });
    return;
  }
  if (renderer === "terminal") {
    await runTerminalTour(tour, root);
    return;
  }

  const output = process.env.CODETOUR_TEST_HTML_OUTPUT ||
    path.join(os.tmpdir(), "codetour-" + randomUUID() + ".html");
  const contexts = tour.steps.map(step => resolveReadonlyStepContext(root, tour, step));
  const html = await createStandaloneTourHtml(tour, contexts, {
    // The browser is a real HTML surface: the sanitized SVG stays sharp at
    // every zoom level, unlike the terminal's half-block preview (ADR 0024).
    renderStepDescription: async description => {
      const { images } = await readTourImages(root, description);
      return renderDescription(description, "dark", {
        diagramFormat: "svg",
        resolveImageBytes: imagePath => images.get(imagePath)
      });
    }
  });
  await fs.writeFile(output, html, "utf8");
  if (!process.env.CODETOUR_TEST_HTML_OUTPUT) {
    await openFileInBrowser(output);
  }
  console.log("CodeTour: opened " + tour.title + " (" + output + ")");
}
